Czestochowa Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Częstochowa, Poland

Not demolished. Jews began settling in Częstochowa in the 18th century; by 1921, 22,663 (28%) were mostly killed during WWII. This cemetery, established in 1808 and gradually enlarged with an embankment, fence, and funeral house, holds the graves of tzaddikim Pinchas Menachem Eliezer Justman (d. November 20, 1920) and Awigdor Szapiro (d. March 10, 1928). During WWII, Germans conducted mass executions here - at least 1,000 people shot in June 1943, about 500 more in July 1943 - and used matzevot for construction. Postwar, the Congregation for the Jewish Faith repaired the wall and demolished the ruined funeral house, marking identified victim graves; a 1946 funeral buried Szmul Rembak and Dawid Józef Gruszka, both killed en route from the Kielce pogrom. The last funerals occurred in 1970. A 1953 ironworks annexation claimed 2.5 hectares, though further expansion plans were never realized. Since the 1980s, the Landsmanshaft of Częstochowa Jews and city authorities have led ongoing restoration.
